```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A tile map describes which small terrain image belongs at each position in
a grid. **shinyphaser** loads maps exported from [Tiled](https://www.mapeditor.org/)
and displays them with Phaser. Start with a tiny room made from two tiles,
then use the Mushroom Swamps map to explore shorelines and larger worlds.

## Start with a tiny room

Before working with Swamps RPG, create an **8-by-6 room** with only two tile
IDs: **1 is floor** and **2 is wall**. Each tile is 64 pixels square. The room
has a border and two wall tiles in the middle:

```text
########
#......#
#..##..#
#......#
#......#
########
```

Here `.` means floor and `#` means wall. A small orange square will be the
player. The complete app, images, and JSON map are already provided in
`inst/examples/simple-map`, so no file-generation step or Tiled installation
is needed.

### Run the example

With shinyphaser installed, run this from the repository root:

```{r eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
shiny::runApp("inst/examples/simple-map")
```

The example contains:

```text
inst/examples/simple-map/
  app.R
  www/
    room.json
    floor.png
    wall.png
    player.png
```

`room.json` contains the 8-by-6 tile grid and two embedded tileset definitions.
Each tileset contains one image, and only the wall tile has the Boolean
property `collides = true`.

### How the app loads the map

The following code is the supplied **`inst/examples/simple-map/app.R`**:

```{r tiny-map-app, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(shinyphaser)

game <- PhaserGame$new(width = 512, height = 384)
ui <- tagList(tags$p("Arrow keys: move the orange square. Walls block movement."),
              game$use_phaser())

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  game <- PhaserGame$new(width = 512, height = 384)
  game$set_shiny_session(session)
  game$set_world_bounds(512, 384)
  game$add_map(
    map_key = "room", map_url = "room.json",
    tileset_urls = c("floor.png", "wall.png"),
    tileset_names = c("floor", "wall"), layer_name = "terrain"
  )
  player <- game$add_sprite(
    "player", "player.png", x = 96, y = 96,
    frame_width = 32, frame_height = 32, frame_count = 1, frame_rate = 1
  )
  player$add_player_controls(speed = 140)
  game$enable_terrain_collision("player")
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Shiny serves the files in the app's `www/` folder, so the URLs above need no
extra resource-path setup. The first loaded map becomes active automatically.
The 512-by-384 canvas matches `8 * 64` by `6 * 64` pixels, and the player
starts in the center of the first interior floor tile.

Try moving across the floor and into both the border and the middle wall.
To change the room, edit the tile-data array in `www/room.json` (1 for floor,
2 for wall), or open that JSON file in Tiled, then restart the app. You now have the same basic ingredients as a larger map: tile IDs,
tileset images, a terrain layer, and an actor registered for terrain collision.
Phaser still loads from jsDelivr, so the browser needs Internet access.

### See the example in action

The orange square moves across the floor and stops at the room's border and
the wall in the middle:

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="512px", fig.alt="Orange player moving through a small tile map and colliding with walls"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/simple_map_example.gif")
```

## Organize the Swamps RPG map and artwork

Swamps RPG uses the same map-loading API, with more terrain variants, a larger
world, and separate scenery. With the current development version installed,
run the full example from the repository root:

```{r eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
shiny::runApp("inst/examples/swamps_rpg")
```

Swamps RPG keeps its map and images together:

```text
inst/examples/swamps_rpg/
  app.R
  modules/navigation_setup.R
  www/
    maps/mushroom_swamps.json
    terrain/mushroom_swamps/
      mushroom_swamps_grass_1.png
      mushroom_swamps_swamp_1.png
      ms_bank_left.png
      ms_bank_left_right.png
      ...
```

Its map is a **finite, orthogonal** grid with 32 columns and 64 rows. Each tile
is 100 by 100 pixels, giving a world of **3200 by 6400 pixels**. The visible
canvas can be smaller: a following camera lets the hero explore the world.

The map's `terrain` layer contains tile IDs in row order, left to right and
then top to bottom. Tiled uses zero-based cell coordinates. Cell `(column, row)`
has its center at:

```{r eval=FALSE}
x <- (column + 0.5) * 100
y <- (row + 0.5) * 100
```

These are world coordinates, not screen coordinates. In R, the corresponding
position in the flat tile-data vector is `row * map$width + column + 1`.

## Create or edit the map in Tiled

1. Create a finite **Orthogonal** map. For the supplied artwork, choose
   100-pixel tile width and height, and a 32-by-64 map to match Swamps RPG.
2. Add a tile layer named **`terrain`**.
3. Create tilesets from the terrain PNGs. Swamps RPG uses one 100-by-100 image
   per tileset, with one tile in each. Embed the tilesets in the map so their
   definitions are included in the exported JSON, rather than external TSX files.
4. Fill the layer with grass, paint swamp areas, and choose bank variants for
   swamp cells that touch grass. Keep the hero's spawn on clear grass.
5. Set a Boolean tile property named **`collides`** to **`true`** on the swamp
   and bank tiles. Grass tiles do not need this property.
6. Save/export as Tiled JSON under `www/maps/`. Use an uncompressed numeric
   tile-data array for the inspection and shoreline code shown below.

Keep the images in their expected relative locations when moving the map.
In Swamps RPG, the JSON image paths start with `../terrain/mushroom_swamps/`,
relative to the map file. The JSON layer name and tileset names must match the
names passed to the R API.

## Understand tile IDs and collision properties

The layer data stores **global tile IDs**, not image filenames. Each embedded
tileset has a `firstgid`. In this example each tileset contains one tile, so
that number identifies its image directly.

| Current ID | Tileset or image | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mushroom_swamps_grass_1` | Walkable grass |
| 2 | `mushroom_swamps_swamp_1` | Interior swamp, without a shore |
| 5 | `ms_bank_left.png` | Swamp with a shore on its left |
| 11 | `ms_bank_top_left_right.png` | Shores above, left, and right |
| 17 | `ms_bank_left_right.png` | Shores on both left and right |
| 18–21 | Remaining grass variants | Walkable grass |

These IDs belong to the current map. Reordering tilesets can change them;
derive IDs from the map's tileset definitions when writing tools.

The collision property is attached to the **tile inside its tileset**. Its
local ID is 0 even when its global map ID is 2:

```json
"tiles": [
  {
    "id": 0,
    "properties": [
      {"name": "collides", "type": "bool", "value": true}
    ]
  }
]
```

Loading this property marks terrain tiles as collidable, but an actor still
needs `game$enable_terrain_collision("hero")` to collide with that layer.
The property must be a Boolean, not the text `"true"`.

## Choose banks from neighboring cells

A bank is still a **swamp cell**. Its suffix describes which sides meet
grass. For example, `left_right` is the correct bank when grass touches both
its left and right sides. Choosing just `left` leaves an abrupt edge on the
other side. `top_left_right` means three shores, not a diagonal corner.

For each swamp cell, examine the four immediate neighbors:

- grass above requires `top`;
- grass below requires `bottom`;
- grass to the left requires `left`;
- grass to the right requires `right`.

Combine the sides and choose the matching variant. No grass neighbors means
the plain swamp tile. Diagonal neighbors do not add sides in this scheme.
Swamps RPG also keeps a shore where swamp touches the outer map boundary.

This helper applies that rule across the map without changing which cells
are grass or swamp. It is specific to Swamps RPG's unflipped, single-tile
tilesets and their naming convention:

```{r bank-helper, eval=FALSE}
update_swamp_banks <- function(map) {
  layer_id <- which(vapply(map$layers, function(x) x$name == "terrain", logical(1)))
  stopifnot(length(layer_id) == 1L)
  original <- unlist(map$layers[[layer_id]]$data)
  updated <- original
  ids <- vapply(map$tilesets, function(x) x$firstgid, numeric(1))
  tileset_labels <- vapply(map$tilesets, function(x) x$name, character(1))
  grass <- ids[grepl("^mushroom_swamps_grass_", tileset_labels)]
  signature <- function(sides) {
    if (length(sides)) paste(sort(sides), collapse = "_") else "interior"
  }
  banks <- grepl("_bank_", tileset_labels)
  keys <- vapply(strsplit(sub(".*_bank_", "", tileset_labels[banks]), "_"),
                 signature, character(1))
  choices <- c(setNames(ids[banks], keys),
               interior = ids[tileset_labels == "mushroom_swamps_swamp_1"])
  grass_at <- function(column, row) {
    if (column < 0 || column >= map$width || row < 0 || row >= map$height) {
      return(TRUE) # Close off swamp at the map's outer edge.
    }
    original[row * map$width + column + 1] %in% grass
  }
  for (row in seq_len(map$height) - 1) {
    for (column in seq_len(map$width) - 1) {
      index <- row * map$width + column + 1
      if (original[index] %in% grass) next
      neighbors <- c(
        top = grass_at(column, row - 1), bottom = grass_at(column, row + 1),
        left = grass_at(column - 1, row), right = grass_at(column + 1, row)
      )
      gid <- unname(choices[signature(names(neighbors)[neighbors])])
      if (is.na(gid)) stop("No bank image for cell ", column, ", ", row)
      updated[index] <- as.integer(gid)
    }
  }
  map$layers[[layer_id]]$data <- as.list(updated)
  map
}
```

Read JSON with `simplifyVector = FALSE` to retain its nested structure. Work
on a copy of the example directory, then save the corrected map there:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# In your own app directory, with the same www/ layout:
map <- jsonlite::fromJSON("www/maps/mushroom_swamps.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
map <- update_swamp_banks(map)
jsonlite::write_json(map, "www/maps/mushroom_swamps.json",
                     auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
```

This changes tile selection only. It preserves the swamp footprint and the
tilesets' collision metadata. If you add new terrain types, adapt the helper
before applying it: this recipe treats every non-grass cell as swamp.

## Load the map through R

The complete small app below reuses the installed Swamps RPG map and artwork.
Save it as `app.R` in a Shiny app directory. It loads terrain, creates the Orc,
and lets you explore with the arrow keys.

The two tileset vectors are derived from the same JSON entries, keeping each
**tileset name** paired with the correct **image URL**. For example, the
tileset `mushroom_swamps_swamp_bank_left` uses the file `ms_bank_left.png`;
their names are not interchangeable.

```{r map-app, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(shinyphaser)

example_dir <- system.file("examples", "swamps_rpg", package = "shinyphaser")
addResourcePath("map-assets", file.path(example_dir, "www"))
map <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(example_dir, "www", "maps", "mushroom_swamps.json"),
                         simplifyVector = FALSE)
tileset_names <- vapply(map$tilesets, function(x) x$name, character(1))
tileset_urls <- vapply(map$tilesets, function(x) {
  paste0("map-assets/terrain/mushroom_swamps/", basename(x$image))
}, character(1))

game <- PhaserGame$new(width = 960, height = 600)
ui <- tagList(tags$p("Explore with the arrow keys. Swamp and banks block movement."),
              game$use_phaser())

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  game <- PhaserGame$new(width = 960, height = 600)
  game$set_shiny_session(session)
  game$set_world_bounds(map$width * map$tilewidth, map$height * map$tileheight)
  game$add_map(
    map_key = "mushroom_swamps",
    map_url = "map-assets/maps/mushroom_swamps.json",
    tileset_urls = tileset_urls, tileset_names = tileset_names,
    layer_name = "terrain"
  )

  hero <- game$add_sprite(
    "hero", "map-assets/sprites/hero/orc/hero_orc_idle.png",
    x = 100, y = 100, frame_width = 100, frame_height = 100,
    frame_count = 29, frame_rate = 4
  )
  hero$set_body_size(32, 18, offset_x = 34, offset_y = 72)
  hero$add_player_controls(speed = 220)
  hero$follow_camera()
  game$enable_terrain_collision("hero")
  game$activate_map("mushroom_swamps", player_name = "hero", x = 100, y = 100)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

`add_map()` loads the named layer asynchronously; the first map is activated
automatically. `activate_map()` explicitly selects a map and can reposition
an existing hero. In Swamps RPG, the New game action calls it after setup.
Register terrain collision for each enemy as well if it should respect the map.

The supplied loader renders the layer selected by `layer_name`. A Tiled map
may contain other layers or objects, but this call does not automatically
turn every Tiled object into a shinyphaser sprite or collision rectangle.
Swamps RPG creates actors and scenery separately through R.

## Add scenery and check the result

Trees and bushes are separate images with their own footprints, rather than
terrain tiles. This lets their foliage cover the hero while their bases block
movement. See [Walk behind scenery and block its footprint](scenery-and-collision.html)
for `set_body_size()`, `set_depth_by_y()`, and invisible collision rectangles.

After editing a map, check that:

- the JSON and every tileset image load without 404 errors;
- `terrain` and the tileset names match the R setup;
- the spawn is on grass and leaves room for the hero's collision body;
- every bank includes all sides that touch grass;
- grass remains walkable, and swamp and banks stop the hero;
- the camera can reach the full map and the world bounds match its dimensions.

The package's `test-swamp-banks.R` checks bank selection across the entire
example map. Its scenery tests separately check that tree and bush images
stay on grass. These checks catch different mistakes: correct shoreline
artwork does not by itself guarantee correct collision or scenery placement.
